caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 464 of 2011
lawyer:
Bishmadeb Chakraborty, Deputy Attorney General instructed by Mrs. Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on- Record ----- For the Petitioner 
Rokanuddin Mahmud, Senior Advocate instructed by Mvi. Md. Wahidullah, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Respondent
parties:
The State represented by Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka ----- petitioner
Vs.
Ahmed Akbar Sobhan @ Shah Alam ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J.:- This Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal, at the instance of the State, is directed against the judgment and order dated 22.06.2011 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7930 of 2011 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure making  the rule absolute and thereby quashing the judgment and order dated 07.07.2008 passed by the Metropolitan Special Tribunal No. 2, Dhaka in Foreign Currency Regulation Tribunal Case No. 4 of 2008 arising out of G.R. Case No. 110 of 2007 corresponding to Gulshan Police Station Case No. 61 (02) 07 dated 19.02.2007 convicting the accused-respondent herein under section 23 of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947 and sentencing him to rigorous imprisonment for 2 (two) years and also to pay a fine of Tk. 10,000/-, in default, to suffer simple imprisonment for further 3 (three) months. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, was that on 04.02.2007 at 1.00 A.M. the joint forces raided the residence of the accused-respondent and seized some foreign currencies amounting to U.S. dollar 20857/79 from there and thereafter one inspector of police lodged an F.I.R. with Gulshan on the allegation that the said foreign currencies were imported and kept illegally by the accused-respondent and his other family members. On the basis of the said ejher the case was started and the police, after investigation submitted charge sheet against the present accused-respondent and his wife and three sons under section 23 of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947 read with rule 19T (1) and 19T (5) of the Emergency Power Rules. 2007. 

 3. The case was ultimately transferred to the Metropolitan Foreign Exchange Regulation Tribunal No. 2, Dhaka for trail. This tribunal held trial against the accused persons after framing formal charge against them under section 23 of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947. All the accused persons being absconding could not be read over and explained the said charge. However the prosecution examined 15 witnesses before the tribunal to prove the charge against the absconding accused persons and the tribunal, on consideration of the evidence adduced by the prosecution and other facts and circumstances, convicted and sentenced the present accused-respondent and others as mentioned above. 

 4. The accused-respondent being aware of the said judgment and order surrendered before the court and obtained hail and thereafter he filed the above mentioned Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7930 of 2011 under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure praying for abashment of the said judgment and order of conviction and sentence and obtained rule. A Division Bench of the High Court Division after hearing both the parties made that rule absolute and quashed the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence on the main ground the impugned proceeding initiated against the accused-respondent was in violation of section 23 of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947. The High Court Division, on elaborate discussion made observation to the effect that the lodgment of the FIR. by a police inspector, submission of the charge sheet and taking of cognizance by the tribunal on the basis of the said F.I.R. and the charge sheet, being contrary to and in violation of the requirements of section 23 (2) (3) of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act are had in law. The High Court Division observed also that the proceeding was not initiated by a person duly authorized either by the Government or Bangladesh Bank as required under section 23 of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947 and as such the same was a nullity. The High Court Division referred to a decision of the Appellate Division in the case of State Vs. Mirza Abbas reported in 15 DLR (AD) 141. The High Court Division made comment to the effect also that a person is authorized by law to keep upto U.S $ 5,000/-, but in the instant case much less then U.S. $ 5,000/- were recovered from the joint possession of 5 accused persons and, therefore, on offence at all was committed. 

 5. Mr. Bishmadeb Chakraborty, the learned Deputy Attorney General though has appeared before us to place this criminal petition for leave to appeal but have frankly has conceded that the above observations and findings of the High Court Division, being correct, do not call form interference. The learned Deputy Attorney General also has referred the judgment passed by this Appellate Division in the case of State Vs. Mirza Abbas reported in 15 MLR (AD) 141 and has submitted that the apex court of the country has already settled that for contravention of any of the provisions of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947 proceedings are to initiated on presentation of complainant by a person duly authorized either by the Government of by the Bangladesh Bank. The learned Deputy Attorney General has conceded that the F.I.R. on the basis of See which the case was started and the court took cognizance of the case was filed by a police officer who was not at all authorized either by the Government of by the Bangladesh Bank to lodge that F.I.R. and in the circumstances the whole proceeding was illegal.
